issues.description: Entire compiled script transported through RPC payload instead of a download endpoint
issues.detail: The algorithm chosen is: read whole file into memory, JSON-encode it, ship over RPC, hold it in React state, re-encode as Blob. For a pipeline script this is O(n) memory in three places with no streaming. A dedicated download/read-file endpoint keyed by pipeline_package_path would be the right data structure. WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE.

issues.description: open() lacks explicit encoding and binary-safety reasoning
issues.detail: with open(script_path) as f: f.read() relies on the platform default encoding, which is not stated as an invariant of compile_pipeline's output. State the invariant: the compiled script is UTF-8 text. Then write open(script_path, encoding='utf-8'). Otherwise this is correct-on-my-machine, not correct. UNDER-AUDITED.

issues.description: Download handler lacks a literate comment explaining the create-anchor-and-click idiom
issues.detail: handleDownloadClick performs a well-known but non-obvious browser dance: Blob -> object URL -> synthetic anchor -> click -> revoke. A two-line comment stating the invariant (URL is revoked on every exit path; anchor is removed even on error) would make this readable as literature rather than copy-paste. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: Object URL and DOM anchor not revoked on exception path
issues.detail: If a.click() throws (rare but possible under CSP or sandboxing), removeChild and revokeObjectURL never run, leaking a Blob URL and an orphan node. Wrap in try/finally so the cleanup invariant holds unconditionally. Small, but exactly the kind of off-by-one-on-control-flow a careful reader would flag.

issues.description: Filename derivation uses split('/').pop() without auditing the input shape
issues.detail: props.compiledPath comes from os.path.relpath on the server; on Windows-hosted notebook servers the separator could be backslash, making split('/').pop() return the full path. Either guarantee forward-slash at the server boundary (state that invariant) or split on both separators. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-WRONG on non-POSIX hosts.

issues.description: GetAppIcon is interactive but not a button (no role, no keyboard handler)
issues.detail: An onClick on a bare SVG icon is not reachable by keyboard and exposes no accessible role. Wrap in a <button> or IconButton with aria-label. This is the readable-to-the-reader (and to the screen reader) constraint; the compiler accepts the current form, the user of assistive tech does not.

review.summary: The feature is small and largely correct, but the chosen data flow — read whole compiled script on the server, embed in RPC JSON, store in React state, re-blob on click — is the wrong data structure for what is conceptually a file download; a path-based fetch endpoint would be more honest. The Python read lacks an explicit encoding invariant. The client-side download idiom is the standard create-anchor-and-click pattern but ships without a literate comment, without try/finally cleanup, without cross-platform path handling, and without an accessible button wrapper. Decision: UNDER-AUDITED with one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE concern; none of the issues block merge for a lab extension, but each is the kind of detail a careful reader would want resolved before this code outlives its author.
